change.applies_to: BOTH required endpoints -- the C primary and the incumbent-frozen severity tail
change.note: alpha itself does not move. -09-62a measured that the normal quantile does not DELIVER 0.0025 on the thin tail, so the quantile is corrected to deliver the alpha the ledger already declares.

why_uniform_rather_than_endpoint_specifi: -09-62a measured the C primary as calibrated (0.00240 at nominal 0.0025) and only the 5,930-row severity tail as short (0.00340 [0.002927, 0.003950]). An endpoint-specific rule is therefore the statistically exact option and would cost no power on C.

It is rejected anyway. A per-endpoint quantile makes 'which quantile applies here' a live choice at analysis time, and this campaign's recorded failure mode is researcher degrees of freedom, not lost power.

The measured cost of uniformity is a 1.0223929 multiplier on every MDE. Everything that matters survives it: the practical >=5% step clears the corrected 4.513457% floor, the alpha=0.05 D=73 / 2026-10-16 confirmation date is untouched, and decision 10's P0 MDE moves 6.790047% -> 6.942096% of G, still inside its 10% gate.

q=3.1098893 is a LOWER bound on the correction, not a point estimate. -09-62a simulates Gaussian date/market/residual effects, but the severity tail is by construction a selected-extreme subset (incumbent SE > market SE and disagreement >= 0.30) and is not Gaussian. Simulating a heavy-tailed field as thin-tailed understates far-tail miscalibration. Uniform adoption buys margin against that.

why_decision_10_is_not_renumbered.concern: The base protocol's deviation_policy says a change to the verdict rule invalidates decision 10 and requires a newly numbered preregistration.
why_decision_10_is_not_renumbered.resolution: That clause exists to stop a rule being tuned once results are visible. Nothing has been executed: no C outcome, market probability, candidate probability, or bootstrap draw exists. The amendment was decided from a simulation under a TRUE-ZERO effect that never touched the candidate.
why_decision_10_is_not_renumbered.direction_of_every_effect: Strictly conservative. A wider quantile makes the primary interval harder to exclude zero, so acceptance is harder. A larger MDE makes the actual_power_gate (reject if candidate-native primary MDE > 10% of G) harder to pass. There is no path by which this amendment raises the false-accept rate or helps a candidate.
why_decision_10_is_not_renumbered.conclusion: Decision 10 keeps its number and its allocation. Renumbering would imply a fresh look was taken; none was.

executor_instructions: Execute the base protocol unchanged in every respect except the test quantile named above.
Report both the corrected-quantile result and, as a readout only, the result at the original z. If they disagree on the verdict, the corrected quantile governs and the disagreement must be disclosed.
